to_five: hs land: when the land is undone by a concurrent land, automatically sync and re-land (re-running --check) instead of exiting 1, at least when the only overlap is merge=union files like NOTES.md

Make `hs land`/`hs sync` print what they are fetching and from whom, time out after ~20 s with the missing object named, and keep `hs status`/`hs log` purely local; with that I would have landed in seconds (git push would have).

`hs watch --path X` (and `hs claims`) should report the owner's presence/WIP for that path (e.g. 'a2 online, editing /src/scheduler.js uncommitted, last seen 10s ago') so waiting on a dependency is informed.

When a land touches /.hsreview-protected paths, hs land should land the unprotected files and turn the protected ones into a proposal to the required reviewers in one step (e.g. hs land --split-review). Missing-block errors should retry or wait for the hub instead of failing immediately, and should agree with hs doctor.

hs should fetch the missing main-view blocks from the connected hub automatically on any command (hs fetch with progress and a timeout as the fallback), and hs doctor should flag it, so a connected hub never leaves the worktree unusable.

hs land should fetch missing index blocks from the hub itself (retry until timeout) instead of failing, and an approval event should only print 'approved' when the current revision actually counts it (show 'approved rev 0, rev 1 needs re-approval' otherwise)
hs land --split-protected: land the unprotected paths now and automatically open a proposal (reviewers taken from /.hsreview) for the protected ones, landing it when approved

When a provisional land is dropped or never reaches a holder, hs status / next command / feed should print '!! your land #57 was lost (never reached a holder): run hs land' and auto-retry it on the next online command; and hs land --paths to land files independently of a pending proposal.

When a land touches /.hsreview paths without approval, land the rest and auto-create the proposal for the protected paths (e.g. hs land --split-protected: 'landed #87 (5 files); proposed P3 for /CONTRACTS.md, asked ann').

Make `hs land` do the --split itself when the only blocker is a /.hsreview-protected path (land the rest, propose the protected files, print 'P1 proposed to ann'), and check that protection before running --check.

`hs land` on an approved proposal whose protected file only changed by a clean merge of teammates' already-approved hunks should land it (approval pinned to my hunks, not the whole file); otherwise it should re-propose itself and `hs land --wait-final` should wait for the new approval instead of failing.
hs land --item <id> --split: land the unprotected files now under the item, propose the protected ones, and close the item automatically when the approved proposal lands
`hs wait-final [#n]` (default: my last land): block until it is final, printing hub stall/recovery, exit 0 when final, 2 on timeout, so you don't have to re-run land or poll status
hs watch --path <file> --count 1 --sync: once the wait ends, sync it into the worktree and print the changeset message, so waiting for a teammate and getting their work in is one command

hs land, when it merges teammates' changes into an approved /.hsreview file, should print 'approval kept: merged lines from #105 (approved P? / author-bound)' or 're-review needed', so I know the contract ann approved is the one on main.

hs watch --path: when the path changed at or before the synced base and the wait would otherwise block, print 'already in your files: #58 pm /CHANGE-REQUEST.md' and exit 0 (or warn up front), so a wait never blocks on something you already have

`hs land` should always split: land files outside /.hsreview immediately and update the workspace proposal to cover only the protected paths (P1 = /CONTRACTS.md only), instead of tying every file in the workspace to the open proposal.

hs land (or the running hs watch) should auto-re-land a provisional land that gets undone by a reorg, keeping the same --check, and report `#51 re-landed as #N`, so an undo never needs the author to notice.

hs claims / hs watch --for-me should tell each agent whether a change request assigns them anything (e.g. 'CR-1: no part for a1'), so an agent with no part knows it is done without reading the CR text

hs land, when a split would update an already-approved proposal, should warn and offer to land the approved revision first (e.g. land approved P1 rev 0, then propose only the new lines as P2) instead of silently resetting approvals

hs land --check, on failure: print 'new since your base: #72 a2 /src/scheduler.js ...' for incoming changesets the check read, plus the last 10 lines of the check output, so the cause is obvious without digging

hs land: merge adjacent-but-distinct markdown sections (by ## heading) in files like CONTRACTS.md automatically instead of stopping with 'real conflicts', showing the merged section boundary in the output

hs watch --path

--count 1 --sync should count only changesets after my synced base that are not mine and not already in my files, so it neither returns at once on my own land nor skips lands made between my sync and the start of the wait

hs land --item C… should say 'this closes C… (whole item); add --under C… to land a piece and keep it open' before closing an item whose title covers more than the changeset, or `hs claim --done` should be the only way to close a self-created item.
`hs watch --item <id> --claimed` (or have `hs claims --wait`) that blocks until the item has a lead and prints who it is, so deciding whether to defer needs no polling.
Make `hs watch --path X --count 1 --sync` print the item and its lead when the matched changeset carries one (e.g. 'item Cc91ec1, lead a3'), and drop the 'run hs sync' hint when --sync already synced

hs watch --path X --sync: when the change is already on main, just say 'already landed (#2), synced' and drop the 'run hs sync' hint; plus show the item text in `hs claims` so ownership is clear without reading the file
`hs watch --item C31ca6b --sync`: block until a land linked to the item (or its --done) arrives and sync it, so non-leads can wait on the work itself rather than guessing a --path
hs claims (and the feed) should show linked lands under an item, e.g. 'C31ca6b lead a3 — landed #6 (linked), not marked done', so teammates can tell a CR is on main without reading messages
hs claim <item> should push a follow-up to every claimant when another claim arrives (e.g. feed line '@ C31ca6b: a1 claimed after you; you lead') and hs claims should list all claimants in order.
`hs land`/`hs sync` print an explicit `!! new unclaimed task on TASKS.md: CR-1` when incoming changes add a task line nobody has claimed.
`hs tasks` (open/claimed/done parsed from TASKS.md) plus `hs watch --claim CR-1` that blocks until someone claims it and prints who.

`hs claim <item>`: append the claim line to TASKS.md, land it, and print 'you hold CR-1' or 'CR-1 already claimed by a2 (#5)' based on settled order; skip the untested warning for merge=union-only lands.
hs claim exits non-zero when another agent leads, and land only links to an item with explicit --item (or says why it linked and that it won't close it)
hs claim <item> --review: record non-lead claimants as reviewers, show it in hs claims, and auto-request their review on the lead's --item land
`hs claim <item>`: an atomic first-wins claim on TASKS.md that rejects the land and names the current holder if the item is already taken on main.

`hs claim <task-id> -m ...`: lands a claim line on the task board; if an earlier changeset on main already claims that id, it refuses with '!! <id> already claimed by <author> (#n)' and exits 1, so first-claimer-wins is enforced by hs instead of by agents reading TASKS.md after the fact.
hs claim <item>: atomically appends the claim to TASKS.md only if no earlier changeset on main claims that item, else exits 1 with '!! <item> already claimed by a2 (#3)'

hs claim --new "<title>" should detect an open item matching the title or the just-landed CHANGE-REQUEST changeset and say 'C565eae looks like this, lead a2: hs claim C565eae?' instead of creating a duplicate
`hs watch --path ... --sync` (and the feed) should print new items with their IDs (e.g. `new item C565eae "CR-1" (open)`), or `hs claim --wait-new` should block until the next item opens and claim it
`hs claim --new` detects an existing open item for the same change request and offers to join it instead of creating a duplicate; `--release` reports the remaining lead
